title: Lavender and Epsom bath salt
subtitle: A muscle-soothing bath blend
excerpt: Epsom salts and sea salt with lavender essential oil and dried lavender flowers, for a bath after long days or exercise. The magnesium sulphate in Epsom salts relaxes tired muscles. Makes 500 g, enough for five baths.
sourceNotes: Epsom salts (magnesium sulphate) in bath preparations: general spa and balneotherapy reference. Note on transdermal magnesium absorption: the evidence for significant transdermal absorption of magnesium from bath salts remains limited and contested; this recipe describes a traditional preparation rather than a therapeutic claim. Lavender essential oil first-trimester caution: EMA HMPC monograph on Lavandula angustifolia (2012).

recipe.yieldDescription: ~500 g bath salt blend (5 baths at 100 g per bath)
recipe.batchNotes: Make 1 kg for a larger supply; keep the same proportions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix a batch and keep it in a sealed jar by the bath.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps one year in a sealed jar in a dry bathroom cupboard. The lavender scent fades over four to six months; the salt blend itself is indefinitely stable. Use a dry scoop to avoid introducing moisture. Discard if the salt clumps solidly or smells off.

glossaryTerms.definition: Magnesium sulphate heptahydrate crystals. Long used as a bath additive in European spa tradition. Dissolves readily in warm water and leaves the bath water feeling silky. Commonly used in bath preparations intended for tired or aching muscles.

content.text: This is a dry salt blend for the bath.

(magnesium sulphate) dissolve readily in warm water and give a slightly silky bath. The coarser sea salt adds body. Dried lavender flowers float in the bath; strain them out before pulling the plug or scoop into a muslin bag before adding. The lavender essential oil carries through the steam.
Lavender essential oil is toxic to cats. Use an unscented bath soak if cats share the bathroom.

items.prepNote: coarse spa-grade sea salt; 30% of blend
optional; add to a muslin bag before the bath to avoid clogging the drain
approximately 80 drops; stir in and let the salt absorb before sealing the jar

content.text: Combine the Epsom salts and sea salt in a bowl. Stir well.
Add the lavender essential oil a few drops at a time, stirring each time so the oil spreads evenly through the salt.
Stir in the dried lavender flowers if using.
Spoon into a sealed jar. Leave the lid slightly open for one hour so the oil absorbs into the salt crystals, then seal.
Scoop 100 g under the running tap as the bath fills. The salts dissolve quickly in warm water. Soak for 15 to 20 minutes.
Keeps one year in a sealed jar in a dry cupboard. Use a dry scoop; moisture causes clumping. The lavender scent is strongest for the first four months.
